pr.title: Plan per-session numbering for inbox items
pr.head: cfbfdf8e8c884005e6201cd241d1cf86a4f51d70

summary: The inbox is where an agent leaves you questions and notices. An agent posts one with the ask or tell tool in Claude Code, or with project inbox ask or tell from the shell. Projector's band, the strip it draws above the Claude Code prompt, lists the items so you can answer or dismiss them. The inbox plan in docs/projects/inbox/readme.md describes that system. It stays in-progress with priority now.

This pull request changes only documentation. It adds two sections to the plan. Then it brings the rest of the plan, the completed questions plan, the README, and docs/plugins.md in line with what has shipped.

• § 10, the band after layer 2. It records five changes the owner decided after using the band, which #295 builds. discuss quotes an item and leaves a blank line under the quote. The drawer loses its Type something field. A quote followed by trailing spaces still counts as ending its line. A resolved item stays for 30 seconds, drawn in the subtle color. /projector takes no argument.
  • § 11, numbering items 1, 2, 3. Today an item's reference names its pull request, such as #337.3. § 11 replaces that with one count per session that covers both questions and notices. It removes project inbox context, the command that explains a reference you type in a prompt, and it migrates no old items.
A plan at in-progress claims to be ready to build, so every question these sections raise must be answered or explicitly deferred. The new § 7 entries defer three follow-ups by the owner's decision.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Item: a question, which you answer or dismiss, or a notice, which you dismiss.
  • Reference: the handle the CLI prints for an item today, such as #337.3, octo/web#12.1, or q2. § 11 replaces it with a number, such as 3.
  • Session: one Claude Code session. Its items live in their own directory under ~/.local/state/projector/inbox/.
  • Drawer: the panel that opens under an item in the band, with its detail, its options, and discuss | dismiss | snooze.
  • discuss: the drawer button that quotes the item's subject in your prompt.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: Projector's review read two heads. At 5a30365 it found one gap. § 10 removed /projector <tracked file> but kept the toast that tells you to run it when the band cannot read a watcher's --tracked path. cfbfdf8 answers that: the toast now says the band does not list the loop, and runningLoops and expandPath go. The review of cfbfdf8 is clean, with four suggestions in its body.

groups.title: The inbox plan
groups.kicker: § 10 and § 11 are new, and the rest of the plan catches up with what shipped
intro: The inbox plan describes the inbox CLI, project inbox, and the band's view of it. Most of this diff is two new sections: § 10 for the band and § 11 for numbering. The earlier sections change only to point at them or to record what has shipped since.

1. Posting. ask and tell read last from a new count.json, write last + 1, and then write <number>.json. The per-pull-request counts.json, the session repository in session.json, and the git config call that finds that repository all go.
  2. Reading the number. The agent sees it in Asked 3. and in ANSWER 3.a … and DISMISSED 3 …. A shell user sees it in project inbox list. The band shows no number, as now.
  3. Prompts. Nothing reads a prompt for references any more, so the band's mayReference and explain and the CLI's project inbox context are removed.
  4. Old items. The CLI refuses an old reference with exit 65. The item-file check skips an old file, so list, watch, the band, and pruning never see it.

Section 2.5 and the acceptance table in section 4 now describe the band as #295 builds it. A resolved line stays 30 seconds in the subtle color, where it stayed a minute, dim. discuss adds two newlines after the quote, where it added a space.

checks.text: Two other open pull requests touch the same ground. #295 builds § 10, and § 11.9 says to build § 11 after it merges. #293 makes every command except answer refuse a letter, and § 11.2 step 5 relies on that. Projector's review ran git merge-tree against both branches, and neither reports a conflict.

files.note: The plan. Read § 10 and § 11 in full. The other hunks are cross-references and records of what shipped.

checks.text: § 3 records why items are keyed by session rather than by branch. Only the asking session holds the agent and the transcript, one watch loop spans many branches, and a detached head has no branch to key by.

§ 7 gains three follow-ups the owner deferred or set aside: revising an open item in place, answering only under the band's own proposals, and finding items across sessions. Deferred items do not block an in-progress plan.
§ 9's history matches git log. #281, #283, #284, and layer 2 (#279) all landed between the 0.7.14 and 0.7.15 releases. The two-row claim matches the comment above focused in hooks/register.tsx.

The § 10 claims about the current code hold at this head. discuss fills the quote and one space, RESOLVED_MS is 60_000, /projector has the [tracked file] hint, and expandPath has one caller, the /projector handler. adopt toasts run /projector <tracked file> for a path it cannot expand, which this bullet now replaces.

§ 11.1's account of today's code holds. post keeps counts.json and session.json, checkout_repo calls origin_repo, which runs git config --get remote.origin.url, and the prompt hook runs project inbox context only when mayReference matches.

Every session's first item is 1. Session directories are never removed, and each one keeps up to 100 delivered items. So a shell command run with no --session and no PROJECTOR_SESSION will usually find the number in several sessions and exit 67. The plan accepts that and tells you to pass --session.

The band reads items through project inbox list --all --json, not from the files directly. A tighter check in load_items therefore hides old items from the band too. Old file names are quoted, such as %23337.1.json, or start with q, so they cannot collide with 1.json.

The mixed-version claim holds for an older band. Its prompt hook runs project inbox context, which the newer CLI rejects with exit 2, and explain discards any output that does not exit 0. It answers by ${ref}.${letter}, which is 3.a under § 11.

groups.title: The completed questions plan
groups.kicker: A note that its last manual check moves to the inbox plan
intro: The questions plan came before the inbox and is completed. Its acceptance table had a main-screen row, which is checked by hand under tmux, and nobody ran it. The new paragraph in § 9 says the inbox plan's § 4 carries that check. It also says the row's clause about the Type something field no longer applies, because § 10 removes the field.

groups.title: README and plugin docs
groups.kicker: The README mentions the band, and the plugin docs explain the mcp__projector__ prefix
intro: The README's section on working with coding agents now mentions the band and the inbox, and links the two reference sections. docs/plugins.md explains why the ask and tell tools carry an mcp__projector__ prefix even though Projector ships no MCP server: the hooks module serves them.

files.note: A new paragraph about the band, with links to the inbox sections of docs/plugins.md and docs/cli.md.

checks.text: Both anchors exist at this head: ### Read your inbox in Projector's band in docs/plugins.md and ## Use the inbox in docs/cli.md.
